rejected.title: Tangent properties
card: A tangent is a line that touches a circle at exactly one point. That point is called the point of contact.
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact. The angle between them is \(90^{\circ}\).
Two tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point outside it. The two tangents are equal in length, measured from the outside point to each point of contact.
Example: tangent \(PA\) is 12 cm and the radius \(OA\) is 5 cm. Angle \(OAP\) is \(90^{\circ}\), so \(OP^{2} = 12^{2} + 5^{2} = 169\), and \(OP = 13\) cm.

2.alt: A circle with centre O at the origin and radius 3. A horizontal tangent line touches the circle at the point P, (0, 3). The radius from O to P is vertical, so it meets the tangent at a right angle.

rejected.remember: A tangent meets the radius at a right angle, and tangents from one outside point are equal.

a.q: A tangent touches a circle at \(T\). The centre is \(O\). What is the size of angle \(OTP\), where \(P\) is another point on the tangent?
a.why: The radius \(OT\) meets the tangent at the point of contact at a right angle, so the angle is \(90^{\circ}\). \(180^{\circ}\) is tempting, but that is the angle along a straight line, not the angle between the radius and the tangent.
a.clue: Think about how the radius meets the tangent at the point of contact.

b.q: Tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\) are drawn from \(P\) to a circle with centre \(O\). Radius \(OA\) is 6 cm and \(OP\) is 10 cm. What is the length of \(PB\)?
b.why: Angle \(OAP\) is \(90^{\circ}\), so \(PA^{2} = 10^{2} - 6^{2} = 64\) and \(PA = 8\) cm. Tangents from one point are equal, so \(PB = 8\) cm. \(\sqrt{136}\) comes from adding the squares instead of subtracting, but \(OP\) is the longest side.
b.clue: The longest side of the right-angled triangle is \(OP\).

version.title: Tangent properties
card: A tangent is a line that touches a circle at exactly one point, called the point of contact.
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so they meet at \(90^{\circ}\).
From a point outside a circle, two tangents can be drawn. They are equal in length, measured from the outside point to each point of contact.
Example: radius \(OA\) is 5 cm and \(OP\) is 13 cm. Angle \(OAP\) is \(90^{\circ}\), so \(PA^{2} = 13^{2} - 5^{2} = 144\) and \(PA = 12\) cm.
version.remember: Radius and tangent meet at a right angle, and two tangents from one point are equal.

a.q: Radius \(OT\) meets a tangent at \(T\), and \(P\) is another point on the tangent. Angle \(TOP\) is \(35^{\circ}\). What is angle \(OPT\)?
a.why: The radius meets the tangent at \(90^{\circ}\), so angle \(OTP\) is \(90^{\circ}\). The angles of triangle \(OTP\) add to \(180^{\circ}\), so angle \(OPT\) is \(180 - 90 - 35 = 55\) degrees. The answer \(145^{\circ}\) forgets the right angle.
a.clue: What is the angle between the radius and the tangent?

b.q: Tangents from \(P\) touch a circle at \(A\) and \(B\). \(PA = 3x + 2\) cm and \(PB = 5x - 6\) cm. What is the value of \(x\)?
b.why: Tangents from one outside point are equal, so \(3x + 2 = 5x - 6\). Then \(8 = 2x\), so \(x = 4\), and each tangent is 14 cm. The answer 14 is the length, not \(x\).
b.clue: Which two lengths must be equal?

wants.brief: A circle with centre O. From a point P outside the circle, two tangents touch the circle at A and B. Radii OA and OB are drawn, with a right-angle mark at A and at B. PA and PB carry matching tick marks to show they are equal.
wants.why: Seeing both tangents with their right angles shows both properties in one picture.
